title: Parts
description: The abstract interaction parts a transport maps wire traffic to and from: part name -> slot name -> slot value. Part and slot names belong to the transport and content components, never to the kernel (shape spec §3.6, contract spec §5.1); this schema fixes only the nesting. See spec.md §4.

Part.title: Part
Part.description: One part: slot name -> slot value.

SlotValue.title: SlotValue
SlotValue.description: The value a slot carries, always wrapped. This is design 2.5's SlotValue unchanged: the same document crosses both boundaries by intent, so nothing translates between them. The wrapper is unconditional because a bare value with a sibling tag would be ambiguous against user data carrying that member (contract spec §5.3).

content.description: The value, represented as 'encoded' says. Absent means the slot was empty; null means the slot carried a null.

encoded.description: How to read 'content': 'json' is the value as it stands, 'text' is a string whose octets are its UTF-8 encoding, 'base64' is RFC 4648 §4 octets (ADR 0006). A transport carrying a body uses 'base64' — it carries octets, not documents (spec.md §4).

content-type.description: The media type declared for this slot, when it had one. Carried so the content component is handed it rather than re-deriving it.

EndpointDescriptor.title: EndpointDescriptor
EndpointDescriptor.description: What a started transport is reachable at: host and port for HTTP, broker and topic details for messaging, whatever else a transport needs. An open document, never assumed to be a URL (spike 1.5 finding 1). Passed to the host unchanged as the 'endpoint' of consumer-session/start-transport.

kind.description: The transport kind that produced this descriptor. Open vocabulary.
